newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech mkts rise on govt moves, but clouds remain.
newsitem.headline: Czech mkts rise on govt moves, but clouds remain.

text.p: Czech capital markets on Thursday reacted positively to a government economic revitalisation package.

Late Wednesday, the government announced sweeping measures aimed at reducing growing budget and trade deficits, while spurring growth, dampening demand for imports and adding confidence to beleaguered capital markets.

Czech equity, debt and foreign exchange markets all gained ground in morning activity on Thursday, boosted by confidence that the measures would help the sputtering economy. But analysts warned that there were still questions over how quickly the package would translate into growth.

"As far as the short-term measures are concerned, the government could hardly do more," said Martin Kupka of Patria Finance. "The question is whether it can be done quickly, to transform these good ideas into real changes," he added.

In releasing the 11-page plan, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said cuts of almost five percent to budget expenditures, limits on public sector wage growth and a speeding up of privatisation would affect almost every Czech.
He said the measures are aimed not only at improving the economy, but also "the completion of the concept of the transformation of the Czech economy".
But Klaus also said that even with the measures, he would consider it a "success" if 1997 GDP growth reached half of the 5.4 percent, year-on-year growth rate forecast in the budget.

The crown, which had fallen some three percent against its dollar/mark basket mid-point in the runnup to the announcement, rebounded strongly crossing into the appreciation side of the basket for the first time since Monday.

Around midday on Thursday, the Czech National Bank (CNB) fixed the crown at 30.081 to the dollar and at 17.415 to the mark implying a deviation from basket parity +0.08 percent, after -0.44 percent on Wednesday.

Traders said investors were pleased that interest and exchange rate policies were not included, though the market is still weary of possible central bank loosening to complement the government's fiscal tightening.

"Everyone is sitting on their hands now because they are focused on what others are doing. When the crown is below the index, it's still a good time to buy the index," said Petr Korous of Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka.

The Prague Stock Exchange also rose, as investors took heart from sections of the plan that pledge a tightening of market regulation, including the creation of an independent watchdog and the separation of investment and commercial banking.

However, some analysts warned that the government must follow through on the plans if the market -- which has been shunned lately by foreign investors because of its lack of transparency and regulation -- is to make a long-term recovery.
"The basic problems here -- ownership of assets and access to cash flows in industry -- have not been addressed at all," said Alex Angell of Wood and Company.
"If they do come through with a high profile SEC chief with definite power to enforce regulations...that might help focus investor intentions," he added.
The bourse's PX50 index rose 0.32 percent at its daily fixing to 553.1.
